raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything fancy. On my 10.7 mu, I’ll still do wheat and maize one after the other, same as most people here. That way the land keeps working all year, and if one crop is not so good, the other can still help the family. I only finished primary school, so I mostly follow what worked on my own fields and what the good farmers nearby are doing. Last few years, when wheat looked weak, a little extra topdressing helped, so I won’t cut fertilizer too hard. But money is still money, so I won’t push too much either. Water from the well costs pumping money, so I’ll irrigate at the key times, not blindly.

For wheat, I’ll sow in early October after maize comes off, use a common improved seed from the local dealer, put most fertilizer as base and then add some urea at jointing if the leaves don’t look strong. Wheat needs water more, so I’ll plan about 3 irrigations if the weather is normal. For maize, the time after wheat harvest is tight, so I’ll keep it simple and sow quickly in mid-June, probably with hired machine help if needed. Maize here usually does fine with one base application and maybe one topdress, and if summer rain is normal I may only irrigate once or even skip if rain is enough. I don’t chase the highest yield. I just want steady grain and not too much cash pressure.
